start.fremd.warum.titel: Why does SCDL restore the files?
start.fremd.warum.p1: SCDL manages the global.ini on its own. This includes translations, header line, strings and blueprints. After every change it stores the file state. If the file is found modified at the next start, it can no longer reliably tell its own changes from foreign ones. Updates and the reset of its own changes could then go wrong.
start.fremd.warum.p2:
If several programs write blueprints into the same file, duplicate or missing entries can result. The programs may also overwrite each other. Faulty translations can affect the generated blueprints as well. Since SCDL also backs up the original texts, differing backup states could restore wrong text passages when resetting.

To avoid this, SCDL resets the global.ini to a defined initial state and then inserts its changes again.
start.fremd.warum.p3:
1. Open INI Injections and choose “Undo blueprints”.
2. Turn off INI Injections under Settings → Add-ons.
3. If the other program provides its translation as a file or URL, add it to the language list under Settings → Languages → globe and select it.
SCDL loads the selected translation itself and adds no blueprints of its own.

dq.titel: Where does the data come from?
dq.tooltip: Where does this data come from?
dq.pipeline: The SCDL pipeline script reads the data from the Star Citizen Data.p4k and prepares it for the SCDL. The developer runs it after every patch, not your PC. The SCDL downloads the result in the background.
dq.ij.bp: Blueprints: Which reward a mission has comes from the SCMDB project (scmdb.net). The SCDL pipeline script translates the missions, adds recipes and reputation, detects duplicate entries in the game data and marks guessed corrections with “(Item corrected)”. It keeps renamed items in a list of their own so completed blueprints keep their tick. Blueprints you have earned come from your Game.log and stay local.
dq.ij.details: Mission details: reputation, reward, cooldown, time limit, prerequisites and players per instance come from SCMDB. Difficulty, instance limits and the time until a new offer are read from the Data.p4k by the SCDL pipeline script.
dq.ij.strings: Text additions: The SCDL pipeline script reads the names of weapons, missiles, components and ships from the English global.ini. The values in the descriptions (damage, fire modes, ammo, resistances) and the rock strength of ores come from SCMDB. The component grade code, e.g. “(Civ/2/C)”, is kept in a maintained list that grows with every run.
dq.overlay: The SCDL pipeline script reads the signature values for rock, salvage and ground from the Data.p4k. Blueprint pool, reward and reputation of the current mission come from SCMDB (scmdb.net). The SCDL reads account balance, signatures and mission titles on your PC with a screen scan.
dq.hangar: Your ships and prices come from the export of the Chrome extension, which you load yourself. Items, slots and the default loadout are read by the SCDL pipeline script from the Data.p4k. The component values come from SCMDB (scmdb.net). The SCDL loads each ship image once from media.robertsspaceindustries.com; the script builds the addresses from the RSI ship matrix.
dq.hangarPreise: Component prices and the shops with their locations are community data from UEX Corp (uexcorp.space) – they are not in the Data.p4k, because Star Citizen keeps shop inventories on the server. Only the SCDL pipeline script queries them, never the SCDL itself. They are estimates and may be out of date; parts without a known price are left blank.
dq.tracking: The SCDL reads statistics and play time from your logs. The SCDL pipeline script reads clear names of weapons and ships and the place names from the global.ini and the starmap data in the Data.p4k. If a name is missing, the SCDL shows the raw name instead of an invented one.
dq.dashboard: The location tile translates places from the Game.log with a list that the SCDL pipeline script builds from the starmap data in the Data.p4k. The hangar tiles show data from your hangar export. The SCDL works out all other tiles from your logs and settings.
dq.joysticks: The SCDL reads your curves, deadzones and bindings from the actionmaps.xml (or the layout file you pick). It only changes there what you save. Function names, factory layouts and the curve tree come from the defaultProfile.xml and the global.ini in the Data.p4k of your installation, without a detour via a server. These values change with every patch. If the Data.p4k is unreadable, the SCDL shows no values rather than guessed ones.
dq.bindings: The SCDL reads your bindings from the actionmaps.xml (or the layout file you pick above). It only contains your changes. All functions, their names and the factory bindings come from the defaultProfile.xml in the Data.p4k of your installation, without a detour via a server. Together they make up the list. The Data.p4k values change with every patch; if it is unreadable, the SCDL only shows your file.
dq.scset: The quality levels and their values come from the CVar groups in the Data.p4k (Engine/Config/CVarGroups). They are stored in the SCDL and updated after patches. Only the user.cfg of your installation is written.

settings.sec.usercfg.desc: The SCDL creates a user.cfg in each Star Citizen installation folder if there is none yet. If one already exists, it checks whether g_language = german_(germany) and g_languageAudio = english are set, and adds them if they are missing. The German language slot is only the carrier, not the content: Star Citizen offers no free slot for custom language files, so the SCDL puts every translation there – an Italian or Japanese one too. bp.helpModal.title: Guide: Earned blueprints
bp.helpModal.body:
This module marks your earned blueprints directly in the game: [x] (already earned) and [ ] (still open) will appear next to each blueprint in mission texts.

Log ScannerFully automatic, but error-prone

The log scanner reads your Star Citizen log files and detects all earned blueprints without any manual input.

1
When you receive a blueprint, Star Citizen writes the entry Bauplan erhalten: into the log files. When the game closes, this file is automatically backed up to logbackups/.
2
The SCDL monitors the current log files in the installation directory while Star Citizen is running. As soon as Star Citizen writes a blueprint entry, it is detected within ~2 seconds and added to the collection without interrupting gameplay. Note: The [x] marker in mission texts will only appear after the next game start, as Star Citizen loads its texts into memory only on startup.
3
All found blueprints are merged with the existing collection and immediately injected into all active Star Citizen installations. A banner with the result will appear in the SCDL.
4
On SCDL start, once you have used the log scan at least once, a full scan of all log files (Game.log + logbackups/) is automatically run so no blueprints earned in the meantime are missed.
Manual scan: Use Import from log files to start a full scan of all log files at any time, for example during initial setup.
Scanned directories:
StarCitizen\LIVE\Game.log
StarCitizen\LIVE\logbackups\*.log
StarCitizen\HOTFIX\Game.log
StarCitizen\HOTFIX\logbackups\*.log
PTU/EPTU are not included. Blueprints are collected across installations in sc_bp_erledigt.json for LIVE/HOTFIX.
Tip: As long as you keep your log files, you can run the scan again at any time across multiple game sessions. Already imported blueprints are stored in sc_bp_erledigt.json regardless, even if you delete old log backups later.
In-game display:
After importing, [x] (earned) and [ ] (still open) will appear next to each blueprint in mission texts. Thanks to Auto-Sync, your markers are automatically transferred to the new global.ini with every language update. You do not need to repeat anything by hand.

Note: Star Citizen loads its texts into memory only on game start. New [x] markers will not be visible in a running game session, but only after the next Star Citizen start.

gt.modal.title: Game statistics
gt.nav.intro: Reads the log files of your installation. The scan only runs when you start it.
gt.leer: The log files say nothing about this.
gt.scan.title: Scan
gt.scan.desc:
This is where the statistics come from. The scan only runs when you press the button.
Files already read are remembered, so next time only the new ones are scanned.
gt.scan.hinweis: Star Citizen keeps only the most recent log files and deletes older ones itself. The launcher therefore stores a summary on every run. Sessions once read stay in your statistics even after the file is gone.
gt.scan.abJahr: Only log files from 2026 onwards are read. Star Citizen changed its log messages several times across builds: older files miss messages entirely or word them in a way today's reader misreads. Numbers from 2025 and earlier would look right without being right — hence the cut. Older files already read are removed again on the next scan. Playtime is not affected and counts all log files, including older ones.
gt.auto.desc: Reads new log files without a button press: about 90 seconds after each game start and once shortly after the launcher starts. Only new files are read.
gt.stats.title: Statistics
gt.stats.nochNichts: Nothing scanned yet. Run the scan and your numbers appear here.
gt.namen.fehlt: Ship and weapon names still show as class codes: the blueprint catalog hasn't been downloaded yet.
gt.namen.kaputt: Ship and weapon names show as class codes: the blueprint catalog could not be read.
gt.waffen.hinweis: Based on attachment log events, not an exact carry/shot statistic.
gt.schiffeVerloren.hinweis: Counted when you are ejected from a destroyed ship. A ship destroyed without you on board is not in the log.
gt.sess.title: Stability
gt.sess.desc: How often the game exited cleanly, how often it crashed, and why the connection dropped.
gt.sess.abbruchHinweis: These are disconnects from the game server (<Channel Disconnected> in the log), not abandoned missions — those are in the Missions area. Every server change creates one entry, so an evening easily reaches a dozen. Server changes and disconnecting yourself are normal operation, not a fault.
gt.tab.name: Name
gt.heat.hinweis: The brighter, the more playtime. A session across midnight counts proportionally in both hours, not entirely in the starting hour.
gt.zone.zeit.hinweis: Time per jurisdiction is counted from entering one until entering the next — the game does not report leaving. The last jurisdiction of a session is therefore not counted.
gt.schiffe.verlauf.sub: One point per month with an ASOP terminal opened ({0} in total). Months without a visit are missing.
gt.qt.title: Quantum travel
gt.qt.desc: Every target selection and every arrival is in the log. They are paired by ship – travel time only counts for a jump that has both.
gt.qt.hinweis: Destinations and departure points appear as location keys in the log ('rs_asmbl_keeger_02'). There is no name catalogue for them – they stay exactly as the game writes them.
gt.qt.treibstoff.hinweis: The value is the quantum drive's estimate before the jump, not the fuel actually burned.
gt.miss.title: Missions
gt.konto.title: Balance history
gt.konto.desc: History of your balance from the balance scan of the overlay bar: balance, net per session and aUEC per hour.
gt.konto.nie: No balance history yet. It comes from the balance scan of the overlay bar and is taken over during evaluation.
gt.konto.ov.text: Balance history comes from the balance scan of the overlay bar. Turn it on and set a reading area in the “Balance scan” tab. Then evaluate once and the data will appear.
gt.konto.leer: The balance history has no session from LIVE or HOTFIX yet.
gt.konto.leerChar: There is no balance history for this character.
gt.konto.demo: Demo data loaded: for viewing only, not saved, gone after a restart.
gt.konto.hinweis: As of the last evaluation. Only what the balance scan reads in the mobiGlas is recorded. Export and import in the overlay modal, tab “Balance scan”.
gt.konto.linie.hinweis: Independent of the period selected above: pick the range here (1D to Max), counted back from the latest balance.
gt.konto.bilanz.hinweis: Green profit, red loss. A session is one game start (one Game.log); it starts at the last balance before it.
gt.miss.desc: What was accepted, completed and abandoned – plus objectives and, where the log names it, the payout.
gt.miss.hinweis: The mission type comes from the internal contract code and is the same in every game language. Ø duration counts finished missions only, and objectives only those the game actually shows. Party data only exists for logs analyzed with this version – for older logs use “Rescan everything”.
gt.miss.belohnung.hinweis: The payout appears as a separate notification without a mission id; it is matched by how close it is to the mission ending. It shows up in only a small share of log files – the total is therefore not your overall earnings. Event missions often pay no aUEC at all.
gt.zone.title: Jurisdictions and zones
gt.zone.desc: The game reports entering and leaving in plain text. Both together give the time spent.
gt.zone.hinweis: These notifications appear in the language Star Citizen itself runs in – German and English are recognised. If a leave message is missing (server change, crash), that stay is not counted.
gt.schiffe.title: Ships, fleet and gear
gt.schiffe.desc: Which ship was in use, how large your own fleet is and what you actually put on.
gt.schiffe.flotte.leer: no ASOP terminal in the logs
gt.schiffe.flotte.hinweis: Fleet size only appears in the log when an ASOP terminal was opened. Without that it stays empty.
gt.med.title: Injuries and medical
gt.med.desc: Star Citizen reports injuries, being incapacitated and medical bed use in plain text.
gt.med.hinweis: A documented substitute for the death detection that disappeared: being incapacitated and using a medical bed are real messages, not an estimate. They too follow the game's language – German and English are recognised.
gt.leeren.frage: Really clear the cache? Everything it holds will be lost: statistics, missions, ships and all other evaluations. Star Citizen deletes old log files on its own – their values only live in the cache and will be gone for good. A new scan only finds the logs that are still there. Back them up first with Profile Backup (group "Game statistics").
gt.leeren.spielzeit.desc: Total playtime stays as it is, including hours from deleted logs and a value you entered by hand. When off, it starts at zero and only counts the logs that are still there.

settings.sec.scset.desc:
Star Citizen graphics and display options without the in-game menu.
Changes are written to the game files of the selected channel.
settings.scset.alle.tooltip: Write the values shown here to every channel with a detected installation
settings.scset.renderer.desc: Vulkan is the current Star Citizen default. DirectX 11 is the older path and helps if Vulkan crashes on your card. Stored in GraphicsSettings.json.
settings.scset.windowmode.desc: Fullscreen usually gives the steadiest frame times, borderless switches to the desktop faster. “Windowed” is the game default.
settings.scset.res.desc: Star Citizen will not show values above your monitor's native resolution.
settings.scset.vsync.desc: Prevents torn frames but costs input response. Usually better off on G-Sync or FreeSync monitors.
settings.scset.fov.desc: The default is 54 degrees. On wide monitors a larger field of view looks more natural.
settings.scset.grp.upscaling.desc: The game renders at a lower resolution and scales up. Gains frames per second, costs sharpness.
settings.scset.upscaling.desc: Native AA renders at full resolution; the percentages say how much is actually rendered. Fewer percent means more frames and a softer image.
settings.scset.upmodel.desc: Only takes effect with NVIDIA DLSS. Transformer is the newer model and needs an RTX card.
settings.scset.uptech.desc: CIG TSR runs on any card. AMD FSR and NVIDIA DLSS need the matching graphics card.
settings.scset.grp.cfg.desc: Extra lines in the channel's user.cfg. The launcher's language lines stay untouched.
settings.scset.maxfps.desc: sys_MaxFPS – 0 means no limit. A cap just below your monitor's refresh rate keeps the card cooler.
settings.scset.grp.qualitaet.desc: Quality levels of individual areas, as in the game menu under "Graphics". An empty field means the game follows its overall level there.
settings.scset.maxidlefps.aria: Maximum frame rate in the background
settings.scset.maxidlefps.desc: sys_MaxIdleFPS – applies while the game window is not in the foreground. 0 means no separate limit.
settings.scset.displayinfo.desc: r_DisplayInfo – shows performance figures in the top right corner. Each level includes everything from the one before: 1 frame rate, frame latency and server frame rate · 2 plus session, shard and CPU load · 3 plus RAM and video memory · 4 plus GPU load and render details.
settings.scset.eigene.placeholder:
one line per command, for example:
con_restricted = 0
settings.scset.eigene.desc: Only key = value, one line per command. The lines the launcher sets itself (sys_MaxFPS, sys_MaxIdleFPS, r_DisplayInfo) are shown here for reference – they are written from the fields above. Invalid lines are reported on save. Not every command still works, Star Citizen silently ignores outdated ones.

si.nav.intro: Hardware and game data that Star Citizen writes into each channel's Game.log.

si.sec.perf.desc: The CPU index measures the main thread (game logic, AI, physics), the GPU index the render thread (pixels, draw calls, shading). Both come from a short benchmark at game start.
si.pi.cpuHint: Measures a short, sequential benchmark at startup – without a loaded game world. It does not reflect performance during gameplay.
si.pi.x3dHint: 3D V-Cache CPUs often show lower values than expected here – the benefit of their large cache only shows during gameplay in dense scenes.
si.pi.gpuHint: Depends on the resolution – the same GPU scores much lower at 4K than at 1080p.
si.pi.compare: CPU and GPU index measure different things and cannot be compared directly. A lower GPU value does not necessarily mean the GPU is the bottleneck – at a different resolution the ratio would change.

joysticks.liste.leer: Everything in this category is at game default.
joysticks.liste.keinTreffer: No adjusted curve matches the search.
joysticks.achse.keine: This curve is not on any axis of this device. Set deadzone and sensitivity on the device axis.
joysticks.herkunft.erbt: Game default: follows the curve of “{0}”.
joysticks.achse.keineKurve: No action with a curve is bound to this axis in the game – a curve here would have no effect. Bind the axis in the game and it shows up here.
joysticks.herkunft.achse: Curve for the whole axis: every change goes to {0} checked action(s) on the “Axis” tab. To edit one on its own, pick it below the axis on the left.
joysticks.titel.achse: Curve for the whole axis. {0} actions sit on it in the game – every change here goes to all that are checked under “Applies to” on the right. To adjust one on its own, open the arrow next to the axis on the left.
joysticks.titel.achseLeer: No action checked. Check at least one under “Applies to” on the right so the curve has an effect.
joysticks.titel.funktion: This curve applies only to “{0}”. Other actions on “{1}” keep their own curve. Deadzone and sensitivity come from the axis and apply to all of them.
joysticks.titel.funktionOhneAchse: This curve applies only to “{0}”. The action is not bound to any axis of this device – the curve takes effect once you bind it in the game.

joysticks.gilt.verschieden: The {0} checked actions have {1} different curves (orange, dashed). As soon as you change the blue curve, all checked ones get it.
joysticks.achse.desc: Applies to every action on this axis. Both values are named as in the game menu.
joysticks.achse.unbelegt: Nothing is bound to this axis in the game. The values take effect once you bind it.
joysticks.achse.geteilt: Also applies to {0}: same ID, one shared entry.

joysticks.analyse.desc: Checks bindings, Game.log and input devices and builds a report you can share on Discord. Your user name and personal paths are removed. The input test guides you step by step: press a button, hands off, move the sticks.
joysticks.analyse.achsen.text: Move every stick, throttle and rotary all the way to its stops, in every direction. “Done” ends early.

settings.mod.bindings.desc: Change key bindings for keyboard, mouse, gamepad and joysticks by pressing the input, including key combinations (modifiers). Own window with an icon in the title bar.

When using an alpha module, be sure to back up your control profiles first (actionmaps.xml under user\client\0\Profiles\default in the game folder).
bindings.title: Bindings
bindings.desc:
All game actions with their bindings. Green marks what the selected file binds itself, yellow what is not saved yet; everything else is the game's default. Click a binding to rebind it, right-click to clear it or restore the game default.

Click a group name to collapse it. Names and keys come from the language set in the game.

bindings.datei.tooltip: Which bindings are edited: the game's active ones or an export from Controls/Mappings
bindings.erfassen.text: Press a key, a gamepad or joystick button, move an axis or click into the field with the mouse. The device follows from the input. After capturing, a click into the field waits for a new input. Esc cancels.
bindings.erfassen.jsWaehlen: Several joysticks possible. Please choose the game number below.
bindings.erfassen.konflikt: In the same group this is already bound to:
bindings.erfassen.modAllein: This modifier key is already bound on its own to:
bindings.erfassen.modAlleinFolge: The combination only works in the game once this binding is cleared.

bindings.geraete.datei: Applies to the file chosen in the “Bindings” tab: {0}
bindings.html.nichts: Nothing to export: no bindings match the current filters.
bindings.html.fuss: Created by SC Desktop Launcher. Grey is the game default, bold is your own binding from the file.
bindings.reset.keine: This file has no own bindings.

bindings.tausch.zuWenig: This file does not list two joysticks.
bindings.tausch.offen: Save or discard the pending changes first. The swap is written right away.

bindings.tausch.text: {0} ({1}) and {2} ({3}) swap their bindings: what was on one device moves to the other. Numbers, curves, dead zones and own names stay with the device. This is written right away, a backup is made first.
bindings.import.text: Takes over one device's bindings from another file of this channel or from a CIG factory layout. Other devices stay untouched. Every row can be deselected; nothing is written until "Save".
bindings.import.leer: The source has no bindings for this device.
bindings.import.unbekannt: The installed game version does not know this action, so it is not taken over.
bindings.export.text: Creates a new file in Controls/Mappings with only the selected device's bindings from {0}. In the game it can be loaded via "Load control profile".
bindings.export.offen: The saved state is exported. Pending changes are not included.
bindings.export.name: Name
bindings.export.nameFalsch: Only letters, digits, _ and -, at most 32 characters.
bindings.export.existiert: A file with this name already exists. Please choose another name.
bindings.mod.desc: Replace a modifier key in all combinations or remove its combinations. Written on "Save".
bindings.mod.paneDesc: Key combinations from your bindings, such as Alt + L. Game defaults are not in the file, so the list only shows what you bound yourself.
bindings.mod.entfernenText: {0} combinations with {1} go back to the game default.
bindings.mod.konflikteText: {0} actions bound to a modifier key alone are cleared. Afterwards the combination only triggers itself.
bindings.mod.offen: {0} changes pending. They show in the "Bindings" tab and are written on "Save".
bindings.mod.uebersprungen: {0} combinations not replaced: they already contain the new key or already have a pending change.
bindings.zuo.desc: Star Citizen decides in the actionmaps.xml which device has which number. If a device is missing at start or reports a new ID after a firmware update, the numbers shift and bindings sit on the wrong device. Remember the order while everything is right. After every game session the SCDL compares it with the actionmaps.xml and reports differences.
bindings.zuo.export: The joystick order only applies to the active game bindings. In the “Bindings” tab, choose actionmaps.xml as the file.
bindings.zuo.kurztext.geaendert: The device numbers changed ({0}). Your bindings now point to the wrong device.
bindings.zuo.kurztext.fehlt: {0} was not connected in the last session. Bindings on it do nothing.
bindings.zuo.kurztext.ersetzt: {0} reports a new ID, usually after a firmware update. Its bindings can be carried over.
bindings.zuo.kurztext.hinzu: {1} now comes before your other devices; their numbers moved back.
bindings.zuo.kurztext.mehrdeutig: Identical devices report the same ID. The actionmaps.xml does not show whether they were swapped. Swap them by hand if needed.
bindings.zuo.kurztext.unbekannt: {1} was new. If everything works, remember the order again.

bindings.zuo.status.datei-unlesbar: The actionmaps.xml exists but could not be read ({0}).

bindings.zuo.status.geaendert: The order has changed. "Adjust bindings" puts every binding back on its device.
bindings.zuo.status.fehlt: A remembered device was missing in the last session: {0}. The bindings stay as they are. If it is missing on purpose (e.g. hidden by HidHide, vJoy/Joystick Gremlin), use “Correct, remember”.
bindings.zuo.status.unbekannt: A new device was present in the last session: {1}. If everything is right, remember the order again.
bindings.zuo.status.hinzu: A new device shifted the numbers: {1}. “Adjust bindings” puts every binding back on its device; the new one stays unbound.
bindings.zuo.status.mehrdeutig: Identical devices share the same ID, so there is no telling which is which. Please assign them by hand via "Swap joysticks".
bindings.zuo.status.ersetzt: A device reports a new ID, usually after a firmware update: {0}. "Adjust bindings" takes over the new device along with its bindings.
bindings.zuo.ersetztText: The device keeps its number, the bindings stay as they are. Only the new ID is remembered, the file does not change.
bindings.zuo.merkenText: The device numbers from the actionmaps.xml are remembered. Only confirm if the bindings sat on the right devices in the game.
bindings.zuo.reparierenText: The bindings move with their device: {0}. This is written right away, a backup is made first.
bindings.zuo.fehler.merken: The order could not be remembered.
bindings.zuo.warnung: {0}: The joysticks of the last session do not match the remembered order. Open Bindings to check.
bindings.zuo.veraltet: The actionmaps.xml or the remembered order changed since this was shown. The check was reloaded, please review it again.
geraete.hilfe: Re-detect devices or ignore a device in SCDL. An ignored device no longer provides input here. Star Citizen and other programs are not affected. To hide a device from Star Citizen as well, a tool such as HidHide is needed.
geraete.hidhideText: If a device is missing or only partly detected, HidHide is often the reason. After a Windows restart or a USB port change, Windows can give the device a new ID and the HidHide rule no longer applies: select the device again in HidHide. Windows also registers Xbox controllers in two ways, and HidHide does not always hide both. Afterwards use “Re-detect devices” here.
bindings.zuo.hidhide: HidHide is installed: see the hints in the device menu at the top.

geraete.ignoriertToast: The device is ignored in SCDL until it is disconnected or the launcher restarts. Star Citizen still sees it.

il.nav.intro: The overlay bar follows every change right away. While this window is open you see it as a preview – switch it off at the top right.
il.icon.desc: Whether the overlay gets its own icon in the title bar. Hiding it does not switch the module off.
il.aussehen.desc: Where the overlay bar sits, how clearly it shows and which values it displays.
il.verhalten.desc: When the overlay bar shows up and how it reacts to the mouse and to events.
il.verhalten.grenze: The overlay bar only sits on top of Star Citizen when the game runs windowed or borderless, not in exclusive fullscreen.
il.set.deckkraft.hinweis: With the mouse over the overlay bar it is always fully visible.
il.set.loghinweis: Values come from the Game.log; signature, balance and mission scan use text recognition. Star Citizen writes mission pay there only for some missions; aUEC income and spending are now almost entirely missing, so the overlay bar no longer shows them – the balance scan reads your balance instead.

How long should the result be shown in the overlay?
0 = stays until the next result.
il.lesen.polster.hinweis: A bit more than drawn is read on every side because the HUD shakes in flight (dotted frame).
il.lesen.bilder.hinweis1: One frame per reading. Fastest, but a misread also shows up in the overlay.
il.lesen.bilder.hinweisN: {0} frames in quick succession per reading, the majority wins. Safer, but up to {0} times the CPU load.
il.lesen.last.keiner: Nothing is read without an area.
il.lesen.last.text: {0}k pixels per frame · approx. {1} ms per reading · {2} % of one core. All scans together: {3} % CPU usage.
il.lesen.last.knopf: Only on button press (no auto scan): {0}k pixels per frame · approx. {1} ms per reading, with auto scan {2} % of one core. All scans together: {3} % CPU usage.
il.lesen.last.ruht: Not reading right now (element not in the bar or details): {0}k pixels per frame · approx. {1} ms per reading, when on {2} % of one core. All scans together: {3} % CPU usage.

il.scan.desc: Reads the signature (RS value) from the screen in scanning mode and shows what is behind it: rocks with their count, salvage panels, wreck debris or ground deposits. Reading happens on a key binding, a controller button, a click on the radar button in the overlay bar or automatically every second. The launcher recognises the digits itself from the pixels of the selected area.
il.scan.taste.aktiv: Active. The shortcut only applies while Star Citizen is running.
il.scan.taste.belegt: Another program already uses this shortcut. Please choose a different one.
il.scan.taste.ungueltig: This key does not work. Allowed: one key (letter, digit, F key, numpad, arrows …) with up to two of Ctrl, Alt and Shift.
il.scan.taste.nichtImBuild: Shortcuts cannot be captured in this build (bindings files missing).
il.scan.dlg.text: Press the combination you want: up to two of Ctrl, Alt and Shift, then one key. Or let the launcher suggest a free combination. Clicking the field waits for a new input. Esc cancels. Gamepad and joystick buttons are set in the "Gamepad" and "Joystick" tiles.
il.scan.dlg.keineFrei: No free combination found. Scanning also works without a shortcut: use the radar button in the overlay bar.
il.scan.dlg.kombiFrei: The combination is free in the game. The key itself is bound with other modifiers, which does not interfere.
il.scan.dlg.bindingsAus: The Bindings module is off. The check used the saved game bindings (defaults and actionmaps.xml).
il.scan.konflikt.gleich: This combination is bound in the game. While Star Citizen runs, the launcher takes it – the game function then stops working:
il.scan.konflikt.grundtaste: Note: the same key is bound in the game with other or no modifiers:
il.scan.konflikt.frei: This combination is free in the game.
il.scan.konflikt.nichtPruefbar: The game bindings could not be checked (bindings files missing or Data.p4k not readable).
il.scan.bereich.bildUnlesbar: The screenshot could not be opened (PNG or JPG).
il.scan.bereich.bildFormat: The screenshot does not match the overlay bar's screen. Please capture the whole screen.
il.scan.bereich.zuGross: The area is too large (at most 2000 pixels per side). Please draw it tighter around the number.
il.scan.bereich.hinweis:
Draw the area tightly around the signature number. There is only one area; a new one replaces the old one.

The dotted frame shows what is actually read: a little more, because the HUD shakes while flying.
The easiest way is "From screenshot" with an image from scanning mode.

"Test read" then checks exactly that screenshot, otherwise the screen as it is now. In the game, scan with the shortcut or button.
il.scan.bereich.ziehen: Drag a rectangle around the signature · Esc or right-click cancels
il.scan.tabelle.fehlt: The signature table is still missing – it arrives with the next catalogue sync. Until then only the number is shown.
il.scan.tabelle.kaputt: The signature table is damaged and is not used. The next catalogue sync downloads it again.

il.scan.fehler.auto: Automatic reading paused: text recognition does not start. Details in the activity log.
il.scan.ctrl.hinweis: Only works while Star Citizen is running and an area is selected. The button keeps its function in the game – ideally pick a free one.

il.scan.kd.istJs: That was a joystick – this sets a gamepad button.

il.scan.schirm.hinweis: Orange: the area read by text recognition.
il.scan.bereit: Ready. Press {0} in scanning mode – the result appears in the overlay bar.
il.scan.nichtBereit.bereich: First select the area around the signature number.
il.scan.nichtBereit.ausloeser: Set a trigger (key binding). Until then, only the radar button in the overlay bar scans.
il.scan.aufloesung.hinweis: Up to WQHD (1440 pixels screen height) the HUD text is very small and often blurry, even more so with an upscaler. Signatures will then probably not always be recognised correctly.
il.scan.ausloeser.hinweis: Shortcuts, buttons and automatic reading only work while Star Citizen is running and an area is selected.
il.scan.art.tastatur.desc: A keyboard shortcut, e.g. Ctrl + Shift + S.
il.scan.art.gamepad.desc: A button on an Xbox-compatible gamepad. It keeps its function in the game – ideally pick a free one.
il.scan.art.joystick.desc: A button on a joystick or throttle. It keeps its function in the game – ideally pick a free one.
il.scan.art.auto.desc: Reads the area every second while Star Citizen is running and only reports new signatures. As long as the image does not change, it uses hardly any CPU.
il.scan.auto.stat.pause: Auto scan paused after 3 errors in a row – it tries again after 1 to 10 minutes.
il.scan.bereit.auto: Ready. In scanning mode SCDL reads the signature every second by itself – the result appears in the overlay bar.
il.scan.bereit.autoZusatz: It also reads every second by itself.
il.set.klickDurch.desc: In game, mouse clicks go through the overlay bar to the game; in the main menu, a click on the pill opens the detail view. When disabled, the click opens it in game too.
il.set.detailZu.desc: A click on the pill opens the detail view. Choose when it closes again.
il.set.detailZu.maus: When the mouse leaves the overlay bar
il.set.detailZu.klick: On the next click on the pill
il.set.nurSc.desc: The overlay bar only appears while Star Citizen runs. When disabled, it also shows the last session without the game.
il.set.hinweise.desc: New events briefly appear as a notice below the pill.
il.set.hervorheben.desc: The pill lights up when you leave an armistice zone, get injured, die or lose the connection.
il.set.sucheLupe.desc: Magnifier at the end of the pill: opens a search field for parts, ships, commodities, blueprints, SCU and scan signatures. Needs the “Search” module.
il.suche.dlg.text: Press the combination you want: up to two of Ctrl, Alt and Shift, then a key. It must not be bound in Star Citizen, or it triggers something there too – or let us suggest a free one. Esc cancels.
il.suche.taste.doppelt: That is already the signature scan shortcut. Please choose another one.
il.suche.taste.leer: No shortcut: only the magnifier in the pill opens the search.
il.suche.alttab.desc: The overlay shows up in Alt-Tab and the taskbar. Alt-Tab to “SCDL Overlay” opens the search field, with no key binding and a free mouse. Esc or Alt-Tab back to the game closes it. Needs the magnifier, windowed or borderless mode only.
il.suche.taste.desc: Opens the search field right in the game, without the mouse or the F key.
il.set.icon.desc: Shows an icon in the title bar that opens these settings. When disabled, you still reach them through the module card in the settings.
il.mscan.desc: Recognises the tracked mission on screen when the log does not name it – the game tracks missions without a waypoint (e.g. clearing an area) without a log line. Independent of the signature scan.
il.mscan.hinweis: Up to 4 areas possible, all of them are read. Drag one area over each spot showing the tracked mission’s title (e.g. top right in the HUD), a little larger for long titles. Read every second while SC is in front and a mission is accepted. The bar then shows only the mission shown here.
il.mscan.schirm.hinweis: Orange: the areas the mission scan reads (numbers as on the right).
il.notiz.platzhalter: Short note, e.g. ore you are looking for
il.notiz.overlay.an: Shown in the overlay – click to hide
il.notiz.overlay.aus: Detail view only – click to show in the overlay
il.mscan.keinTreffer: No title of an accepted mission recognised. Read: {0}
il.mscan.grund.bildUnlesbar: The screenshot could not be opened (PNG or JPG).
il.mscan.grund.bildFormat: The screenshot does not match the overlay bar's screen. Please capture the whole screen.
il.mscan.grund.zuGross: The area is too large (at most 2000 pixels per side). Please draw it tighter around the number.
il.kscan.desc: Reads your balance (aUEC) on screen while the mobiGlas is open – Star Citizen hardly logs income and spending any more. The last balance read is kept until the mobiGlas is open again. Independent of the signature and mission scan.
il.kscan.hinweis: Up to 4 areas possible, all of them are read. Open the mobiGlas, ideally take a screenshot, and draw an area tightly around the balance. Read every second while Star Citizen is running and in front; 3 frames per reading, a single misread does not count.
il.kscan.beachten: Draw the area tightly around the balance including “aUEC” or ¤ – without any label next to it. While the mobiGlas is closed, the scan reads the HUD at the same spot: a number with a unit (e.g. “1,234 km”) does not count, a bare number does. So pick a spot that shows no number without the mobiGlas, and check with “Test read” that the balance is recognised.
il.kscan.schirm.hinweis: Orange: the areas the balance scan reads (numbers as below).
il.kverlauf.hinweis: Every balance read is kept. You find the history of your balance with the net per session in the game statistics (tab “Balance history”), taken over with every evaluation.
il.kverlauf.gt.text: Your balance history is shown in the game statistics. Turn them on to see it. After turning them on, evaluate once and the data appears.
il.kverlauf.grund.kaputt: The file kontoverlauf.json is damaged and is no longer written. Move it out of the overlay-leiste folder to start a new history.
il.kverlauf.grund.format: The file contains no readable balance history.
il.kverlauf.grund.gross: The file is too large (10 MB at most).
il.kverlauf.datei.hinweis: Export: all characters, times as date and time in local time with time zone. CSV uses semicolons, for Excel. Import adds to the history; existing entries (same time, channel, character) are skipped.
il.kverlauf.import.demo: {0} demo entries loaded. They are not saved and are gone after a restart.
il.kscan.keinTreffer: No balance recognised. Is the mobiGlas open? Read: {0}
tutorial.err.speichern: Could not leave the tutorial: the settings could not be saved.
tutorial.settings_btn.text: Paths, languages, modules and startup programs: everything the launcher needs to know. One click opens the settings.
tutorial.update_btn.text: One click installs the translation into all enabled channels and keeps it up to date.
tutorial.injections_btn.text: Blueprints in mission texts, item values and Strings: additions to global.ini, per channel.
tutorial.bp_quicklist.text: Your list of earned blueprints in one click, without opening the injections window.
tutorial.updates_btn.text: Checks right away whether there is a new SCDL or new translations. Otherwise the launcher checks quietly in the background.
tutorial.whatsnew_btn.text: The changes in this version at a glance.
tutorial.suche.text: Click the magnifier or press Ctrl+S. Find settings and sections, solve maths problems, convert cargo and look up ships, parts and commodities.
tutorial.suche_feld.text: A section, setting, question or problem in your own words, typos don’t matter. Arrow keys select, Enter opens the best match, Esc closes.
tutorial.suche_rechnen.text: Type a sum like 12*3 or 1,5k - 200. The result appears at once, Enter copies it.
tutorial.suche_scu.text: =scu calculates cargo in SCU, “150 scu” converts to cSCU, m³ and boxes. Add a ship after it (@Cutlass) to see whether it fits.
tutorial.suche_kacheln.text: With an empty field you see your recent searches and the most important sections. A click opens them.
tutorial.suche_at.text: Use @ to pick ships, parts or commodities and see price and shop. Several @ in one line make a list with a total; with SCU in front you see whether the cargo fits the ship.
tutorial.suche_beispiele.text: Examples by topic. A click puts the example into the field, the tooltip explains it.
tutorial.sysinfo_btn.text: Shows hardware and system at a glance, handy for troubleshooting and support.
tutorial.cache_cleaner_btn.text: Deletes shader and driver caches when the game stutters or shows graphics errors after a patch.
tutorial.profil_backup_btn.text: Backs up keybindings, characters and settings per channel as a ZIP and restores them.
tutorial.game_tracking_btn.text: Reads playtime, missions, ships and account transactions from the log files.
tutorial.joysticks_btn.text: Set deadzone, sensitivity and curves of your joysticks.
tutorial.bindings_btn.text: Change bindings by pressing a key, without starting the game.
tutorial.overlay_leiste_btn.text: An overlay bar above the game with signature, mission and balance scan.
tutorial.hangar_btn.text: Your ships and pledges from the Chrome extension, with images, components and in-game prices.
tutorial.detect_paths.text: Looks for the Star Citizen installation and usually finds the channels (LIVE, PTU …) on its own.
tutorial.set_lang_nav.text: Which translation runs in which channel, and the language of the launcher itself.
tutorial.set_modules_nav.text: Turn features on and off. Disabled modules disappear from the title bar and navigation.
tutorial.set_startprogramme_nav.text: Start other programs automatically when the RSI Launcher or Star Citizen starts.
tutorial.set_look_nav.text: Set the color scheme and the size of the interface. The “Navigation” tab sets what appears in the title bar and side navigation.
tutorial.set_look_navigation.text: Title bar, side navigation or both: arrange icons and entries here and show or hide them.
tutorial.bp_github_nav.text: Adds to the mission texts which blueprints a mission rewards, per channel.
tutorial.bp_import.text: One click fetches the current blueprint data and writes it into this channel's global.ini.
tutorial.bp_mods_nav.text: Reads from the log files which blueprints you already have and marks them in the mission texts.
tutorial.bp_help.text: Explains where earned blueprints come from and how to keep the list up to date.
tutorial.bp_itemstats_nav.text: Adds their values to items in game, such as damage or output.
tutorial.bp_strings_nav.text: Choose Strings and other text additions for global.ini.
tutorial.bp_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.js_kanal.text: Which channel (LIVE, PTU …) you are tuning the axes for. Each channel has its own actionmaps.xml.
tutorial.js_achsen.text: The axes of the selected device. Move the stick and the matching axis lights up. Click one to open its curve.
tutorial.js_kurve.text: Deadzone, sensitivity and curve shape of the axis. Presets such as “Fine” or “S-curve” set it in one click.
tutorial.js_neu.text: Create a curve of your own for a game action, for example only for pitch or yaw.
tutorial.js_geraete_nav.text: All detected input devices. Re-detect devices here or hide one in SCDL.
tutorial.js_analyse.text: Stick jittering or a button not responding? The input test checks the device and creates a report for Discord.
tutorial.bind_nav.text: All game actions with their bindings. Click a binding to rebind it, right-click to clear it or restore the game default.
tutorial.bind_datei.text: Which bindings you are editing: the game’s active ones or an export from Controls/Mappings.
tutorial.bind_suche.text: Search for an action or key to find it quickly in the long list.
tutorial.bind_geraete_nav.text: Whole devices at once: reset them, swap joystick numbers or take over bindings from another file.
tutorial.bind_zuo_nav.text: Windows sometimes numbers joysticks differently. Save the order while everything is right: SCDL reports deviations later.
tutorial.bind_mod_nav.text: A button as a shift key: while held, every other button gets a second binding.
tutorial.il_vorschau.text: While this window is open, the overlay bar shows as a preview, even without the game running. Switch it off here.
tutorial.il_aussehen_nav.text: Where the bar sits, its size and opacity, and which values it shows.
tutorial.il_scan_nav.text: Reads the signature (RS value) from the screen and shows what is behind it: rock, salvage panels, wreckage.
tutorial.il_scan_bereich.text: First mark the screen area where the game shows the signature. Without an area the scan reads nothing.
tutorial.il_kscan_nav.text: Reads your balance (aUEC) from the screen while the mobiGlas is open.
tutorial.il_mscan_nav.text: Detects the tracked mission on screen when the log does not name it.
tutorial.il_verhalten_nav.text: When the bar appears and how it reacts to the mouse and events.
tutorial.js_gilt.text: All game actions on this axis. Ticked ones get the blue curve; dashed orange lines are differing curves.
tutorial.js_kurven.text: Curves of single game actions, filtered by category or found by search. Click one to open it.
tutorial.js_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.js_restore.text: SCDL makes a backup before every save. Bring back the original or an earlier state here.
tutorial.bind_bereich.text: Shows only one group of actions, for example flight movement or on foot.
tutorial.bind_filter.text: Only favourites or only what you bound yourself. Mark favourites with the star of an action.
tutorial.bind_zuo_merken.text: If the assignment is right, save it here. SCDL then compares after every session and reports deviations.
tutorial.bind_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.bind_restore.text: SCDL makes a backup before every save. Bring back the original or an earlier state here.
tutorial.il_position.text: Where the bar sits on screen: one of six corners and centres, or freely movable.
tutorial.il_bildschirm.text: With several monitors: which one the bar appears on.
tutorial.il_notiz.text: Your own text, for example the ore you are looking for. Shown in the detail view or, if switched on, in the bar too.
tutorial.il_darstellung.text: Opacity and size of the bar. The preview shows every change at once.
tutorial.il_werte.text: Top: what the bar shows. Bottom: what the detail view adds. Click toggles a value, dragging changes the order.
tutorial.il_scan_ausloeser.text: How the scan starts: by hotkey, controller button, the radar button in the bar or automatically every second.
tutorial.il_kscan_neu.text: Drag an area tightly around the balance in the mobiGlas. Easiest on a screenshot.
tutorial.il_mscan_neu.text: Drag an area over the spot where the mission title appears, a little wider for long titles.
tutorial.il_verhalten.text: Each switch with a short explanation below it, including streamer mode for the whole launcher.
tutorial.il_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.set_paths_nav.text: Your Star Citizen installations per channel (LIVE, PTU …).
tutorial.set_paths_kanaele.text: The folder of each channel. If a path is wrong, change it here or switch a channel off.
tutorial.set_paths_rsi.text: Path to the RSI Launcher. SCDL needs it to start the game.
tutorial.set_paths_usercfg.text: Shows whether each installation’s user.cfg sets the game language correctly. If something is missing, SCDL adds the line.
tutorial.set_lang_tabelle.text: For each channel the name and source of the language file: a URL, a file from disk or a language from the list.
tutorial.set_lang_globus.text: The globe opens the predefined languages. One click takes over name and source for this channel.
tutorial.set_lang_reset.text: Resets this channel’s language to the default. Nothing is stored until you click “Save”.
tutorial.set_opts_nav.text: How SCDL behaves in the background: updates, autostart and closing.
tutorial.set_opts_bg.text: What SCDL updates on its own at the set interval. When off, it shows a notice instead of installing silently.
tutorial.set_opts_autoupdate.text: Reloads the language file automatically as soon as you quit Star Citizen.
tutorial.set_opts_tray.text: Whether the X quits SCDL or keeps it running in the system tray.
tutorial.set_scset_nav.text: Star Citizen graphics and display options without going into the game menu.
tutorial.set_scset_kanal.text: Which channel you change the values for. They are written to its game files.
tutorial.set_scset_werte.text: Resolution, window mode, field of view, upscaling, quality and FPS limits.
tutorial.set_scset_eigene.text: More commands for the user.cfg, one “key = value” per line.
tutorial.set_modules_liste.text: Switch each feature on or off here. “Open” jumps straight into it.
tutorial.set_modules_addons_tab.text: Extras that are not in the setup: start programs, joysticks, bindings, overlay.
tutorial.set_modules_addons.text: SCDL downloads an add-on from GitHub on request and checks every file. Then switch it on and open it like any other feature.
tutorial.set_sp_liste.text: Programs and scripts that start together with the RSI Launcher or the game.
tutorial.set_sp_add.text: Add a new program. SCDL runs exactly what you enter here.
tutorial.set_look_theme.text: The look of SCDL. Each scheme applies to all windows.
tutorial.set_look_skala.text: Adjusts the size of the interface to your screen.
tutorial.set_look_streamer.text: Hides personal details such as your Windows name, character and location behind [REDACTED].
tutorial.set_look_sprache.text: The language SCDL itself uses. This does not change the in-game language.
tutorial.set_nav_modus.text: Title bar, side navigation or both. The side navigation makes the window wider.
tutorial.set_nav_reihenfolge.text: Drag icons and entries to another place with the mouse, or hide them.
tutorial.set_nav_dash.text: Where the info column of the overview sits.
tutorial.set_backup_nav.text: Back up settings, reset them to default or restart onboarding and tutorial.
tutorial.set_backup_export.text: Save settings as a JSON file and load them back, for example after a reinstall.
tutorial.set_backup_reset.text: Everything back to default, onboarding with the wizard or just the tutorial again.
tutorial.bp_kanaele.text: For each channel, the state of the blueprints in the mission texts.
tutorial.bp_done_log.text: Reads your Game.log and ticks off blueprints you have earned.
tutorial.bp_done_datei.text: Take over earned blueprints from a file, for example from another PC.
tutorial.bp_done_liste.text: All blueprints with ticks: see and change what counts as earned.
tutorial.bp_done_db.text: Opens Star-Head, BPDB or SCMDB to look up where a blueprint can be found.
tutorial.bp_itemstats_teile.text: Crafting info and the item description can be switched on and off separately.
tutorial.bp_itemstats_werte.text: SCDL leaves out deselected values. Dragging changes the order in the description.
tutorial.bp_missiondetails_nav.text: Choose which details appear in a mission description, such as difficulty or time limit.
tutorial.bp_strings_karten.text: Each card is a group of names that get extra info, such as size and class.
tutorial.js_punkte.text: The curve point by point as numbers: input and output in percent.
tutorial.js_rauschen.text: Measures how much the axes jitter at rest and suggests matching deadzones.
tutorial.js_geraete_liste.text: All detected devices. You can ignore a device in SCDL here.
tutorial.js_geraete_neu.text: Plugged in a device but it is not listed? SCDL searches again here.
tutorial.js_analyse_start.text: Guides you step by step through the input test. Afterwards you can copy or export the report.
tutorial.bind_tabelle.text: Click a cell to rebind, right-click to clear or restore the game default. The star marks an action as a favourite.
tutorial.bind_reset.text: Resets all your own bindings of a device to the game default.
tutorial.bind_tausch.text: Two joysticks swap numbers. Bindings and curves move with the device.
tutorial.bind_import.text: Takes over a device’s bindings from another file or a factory layout by CIG.
tutorial.bind_export.text: Creates a file with only one device’s bindings. Load it in the game via “Load control profile”.
tutorial.bind_zuo_tabelle.text: Which device currently has which joystick number.
tutorial.bind_zuo_reparieren.text: If Windows mixed up the order, this moves the bindings to the right device.
tutorial.bind_mod_tabelle.text: Which buttons act as shift keys and which bindings sit behind them.
tutorial.bind_live_nav.text: All detected input devices. Re-detect devices here or hide one in SCDL.
tutorial.bind_live_liste.text: All detected devices. You can ignore a device in SCDL here.
tutorial.il_scan_bild.text: Choose the area on a screenshot instead of in the running game.
tutorial.il_scan_probe.text: Reads the area once and shows what was recognised. That way you check it is placed right.
tutorial.il_kscan_probe.text: Reads the areas once and shows the recognised balance.
tutorial.il_kscan_verlauf.text: Every balance read is kept. History and balance per session are in the game statistics.
tutorial.il_mscan_probe.text: Reads the areas once and shows the recognised mission title.
tutorial.si_kanal_nav.text: One tab per channel with the data Star Citizen writes into the Game.log itself.
tutorial.si_hardware.text: Operating system, graphics API, CPU, GPU with driver and memory from the last session.
tutorial.si_perf.text: How well the CPU (game logic) and GPU (rendering) perform in the game.
tutorial.si_refresh.text: Reads the Game.log again, for example after a game session.
tutorial.si_export.text: Saves the system info as a file.
tutorial.si_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.cc_auswahl.text: Star Citizen’s shader cache and the graphics driver caches. Tick what should go.
tutorial.cc_nuke.text: Deletes the ticked caches. The first game start afterwards takes a little longer.
tutorial.cc_log.text: What was deleted and what failed. Can be copied.
tutorial.cc_ordner.text: Where Star Citizen stores its shaders. The button next to it opens the folder.
tutorial.pb_profiles_nav.text: A profile is a set of user data under one name, for example HOTAS and mouse/keyboard.
tutorial.pb_profile_add.text: Create a new profile. New backups belong to the active profile.
tutorial.pb_ort.text: Where the backups are kept. When you change it, all existing ones move along.
tutorial.pb_groups_nav.text: Which areas go into the backup.
tutorial.pb_groups.text: Tick what should be backed up. Only ticked areas end up in the backup.
tutorial.pb_logs.text: Collects new log files from LIVE and HOTFIX too, each only once.
tutorial.pb_snapshots_nav.text: All saved states, sorted by time. Back up and restore from here.
tutorial.pb_kanaele.text: These installations are backed up. A switched-off one is also left out of automatic backups.
tutorial.pb_import.text: Load a ZIP that was exported on another PC.
tutorial.pb_liste.text: Every backup with its time. Restore a state from here.
tutorial.pb_when_nav.text: When SCDL backs up on its own.
tutorial.pb_when.text: After the game, at startup or before risky changes. Only what changed is backed up.
tutorial.pb_interval.text: Also back up at a fixed interval. 0 turns the schedule off.
tutorial.pb_keep_nav.text: How many old backups are kept.
tutorial.pb_keep.text: Number, age and size. Whatever exceeds a limit is cleared at the next backup.
tutorial.pb_locks_nav.text: Protects files from a Star Citizen update overwriting your settings.
tutorial.pb_locks.text: Every locked file. SCDL watches it and reports when an update has overwritten it.
tutorial.pb_log.text: Shows what happened to the locked files.
tutorial.pb_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.gt_scan_nav.text: This is where the statistics come from your log files. Only new files are read.
tutorial.gt_scan_neu.text: Reads only the log files added since last time.
tutorial.gt_scan_alles.text: Reads all log files from scratch instead of only the new ones.
tutorial.gt_scan_auto.text: Reads new log files without a click: shortly after each game start and after SCDL starts.
tutorial.gt_stats_nav.text: Overview of everything the analysed log files reveal.
tutorial.gt_stats.text: The most important values from all analysed log files.
tutorial.gt_konto_nav.text: History of your balance from the overlay’s balance scan.
tutorial.gt_konto.text: Balance, result per session and aUEC per hour, selectable by month and year.
tutorial.gt_schiffe_nav.text: Which ship was in use, your fleet and equipped gear.
tutorial.gt_schiffe.text: Used and owned ships, plus the fleet size over time.
tutorial.gt_missionen_nav.text: What was accepted, completed and abandoned.
tutorial.gt_missionen.text: Missions with objectives and, where the log names it, the payout.
tutorial.gt_zonen_nav.text: Where you spent time and for how long.
tutorial.gt_zonen.text: Entering and leaving give the time spent at each place.
tutorial.gt_quanten_nav.text: Every destination choice and arrival, paired by ship.
tutorial.gt_quanten.text: Destinations and travel times. Time counts only when start and arrival are in the log.
tutorial.gt_medizin_nav.text: Injuries, incapacitation and med beds from the log.
tutorial.gt_medizin.text: Injuries, affected body parts, treatment tiers and med bed.
tutorial.gt_sessions_nav.text: How often the game closed cleanly or crashed.
tutorial.gt_sessions.text: Crashes and disconnects with their reason, per session.
tutorial.gt_export.text: Saves the statistics as a file.
tutorial.gt_icon_nav.text: Sets whether and how this module's icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.hg_quellen.text: Green means imported: CSV with your pledges, JSON with your fleet. After that you see when you last imported. Import again with the upload icon next to it.
tutorial.hg_suche.text: Searches all tabs at once. The number on each tab shows its matches. Esc clears the search.
tutorial.hg_ueber_nav.text: Your hangar at a glance: key figures and breakdowns.
tutorial.hg_ueber.text: Ships, LTI, pledges and spending. Below: manufacturers, roles, contents by type and spending per year.
tutorial.hg_schiffe_nav.text: All ships as cards with image, insurance, status and price.
tutorial.hg_filter.text: Sorts by date, name, price or manufacturer. Filters by year, type and status (flight-ready or concept).
tutorial.hg_schiffe.text: A click selects the ship and its profile appears on the right.
tutorial.hg_steckbrief.text: Details of the selected entry. For ships also the components, which you can swap right here.
tutorial.hg_breite.text: Drag here to make the profile wider or narrower. With the keyboard: left and right arrow.
tutorial.hg_komp_nav.text: Components bought separately and the loadout of each ship, with values from the game data.
tutorial.hg_komp_gruppe.text: First the components bought separately, then one group per ship. Expand a group to see its slots.
tutorial.hg_komp_wahl.text: Pick a fitting part for each slot. Your choice is saved and the ship shows “changed”. “Reset to stock” undoes everything. Locked fields are built in.
tutorial.hg_komp_liste.text: Saves the ship’s components as an HTML page, with prices and the in-game shops that sell them.
tutorial.hg_pledges_nav.text: All pledges with contents, date and price.
tutorial.hg_pledges.text: The icons show what the pledge contains. On the right: meltable and giftable. A click opens the profile.
tutorial.hg_lack_nav.text: All paints from your pledges, each with the pledge it came from.
tutorial.hg_ausr_nav.text: Armor, weapons and other equipment from your pledges. With game data the type is shown too.
tutorial.hg_mehr_nav.text: Here you find Other, History (pledges by year with totals) and Import data.
tutorial.hg_icon.text: Sets whether and how this module’s icon appears in the title bar.
tutorial.bind_live_neu.text: Plugged in a device but it is not listed? SCDL searches again here.
settings.mod.hangar.desc: Shows your hangar and fleet from the files of the Chrome extension “Star Citizen Hangar Extension”: ships, pledges, paints, equipment and purchase history. Everything stays on this PC.

suche.frage.scu.text: 1 SCU (Standard Cargo Unit) is a cube with 1.25 m edges, so 1.95 m³. 1 SCU = 100 cSCU = 1,000,000 µSCU. Tip: “32 scu” or “3200 cscu” converts right away.

suche.frage.englisch: Why is the game still in English?
suche.frage.englisch.text: Usually the channel is still set to English, or the translation is outdated after a patch. Check the channel under Settings › Languages and fetch the translation again.
suche.frage.englisch.woerter: english german translation missing language wrong
suche.frage.ampel: What does the channel colour mean?
suche.frage.ampel.text: Green: up to date. Yellow: new translation available. Red: error, for example game folder not found.
suche.frage.ampel.woerter: colour color dot yellow red green status channel
suche.frage.bauplan.text: The scan reads the Game.log. If a blueprint is missing, the game ran without a log or the log was overwritten. Run the scan again under “Scan blueprints”.
suche.frage.erz: How much space does ore take?
suche.frage.erz.text: Ore counts in cSCU: 100 cSCU are 1 SCU. A full Prospector holds 32 SCU, so 3,200 cSCU.
